messages:
maya: Quick sync — been prototyping a compact on-disk layout (working name: safebox) to speed warmstart for sharded safetensors models when we have many small shards and limited RAM. Goal: reduce random IO and metadata hit during warmup and make partial warmstart (hotfill) cheaper. Thoughts?

simon: Nice. Is safebox a single-file bundle or a sidecar index + range file?

maya: Single-file container + small index header. Layout idea: global header (version, checksum), shard manifest (names, offsets, compressed sizes), followed by concatenated chunks aligned to 4KB. We keep per-tensor compact header so we can mmap ranges for large tensors and stream small ones.

anya: Two quick concerns: 1) compatibility with existing manifest-first loaders, 2) failure/rollback semantics during atomic swap.

kevin: Microbench data from my local runs (toy 8-shard LLaMA-like): baseline mmap-open-per-shard warmstart = 420ms median; bundle file w/ contiguous layout + prefetch = 210ms median. So ~2x. Not bad.

josh: Do we intend to support gzipped chunks inside the safebox? That changes mmap benefits.

maya: We'll allow optional per-chunk compression (zstd) in the header. For compressed small chunks we stream decompress into page-aligned ring buffer. For large dense weights we keep uncompressed for direct mmap use.

ci-bot: [deploy-bot] Snapshot artifact uploaded: build/weights-safebox/experiment-2026-02-14.tar.gz

anya: On compatibility: loader currently expects either safetensors or safetensor shards + optional manifest. How does safebox integrate with weightsource abstraction?

simon: Suggestion: Add a new WeightDescriptor.type = "safebox" with fields: container_offset, index_offset, digest, flags (compressed, encrypted). Then existing WeightSource.Resolve() returns a descriptor rather than raw path. Loader can pick fast-paths.

kevin: Implementation detail: We should make the index small and preferrably at start so we can inspect container quickly. But index-at-start means we rewrite whole file on pack changes. That's okay for publish-time artifacts. Runtime hot-swap scenario needs atomic rename of new safebox file.

maya: +1 on index-first. Also include a tiny compatibility manifest (compat_manifest.json) that lists constituent safetensors names so tools can still reason about provenance.

josh: How do we handle partial warmstart, i.e., we only need a subset of layers on this host? We can't mmap whole file if it's huge and we have no room.

maya: We'll support two modes: index-first + range reads (seek+pread) to pull only needed chunks; and a streaming fallback that yields chunk iterators. mmap is only used when the host opts-in and has enough addressable space.

anya: Eviction semantics: if we prefetch into the shared weight cache, we need to mark where each tensor came from to support atomic rollbacks. Also permissions for dedup across safebox and plain shards.

simon: Proposal: Add content-addressed chunk ids in the index (sha256 of chunk body). Shared cache keyed by chunk id. Dedup works across plain shards and safebox. Atomic swap via directory-level metadata: write new safebox -> publish new symlink -> update registry. That mirrors existing weight-swap flow.

kevin: Edge-case perf: if many tiny tensors are in safebox (100k tiny params), the index size explodes. We should support a grouping header: group tensors by layer-block and store a single chunk for small params plus an internal micro-index. This reduces index entries.

maya: Good call. We'll define group_type: "microbundle" with its own inner index. The global index can list the microbundle as one entry and the loader unpacks as needed.

josh: What about backward compatibility with model bundles that don't include safebox? Falling back to current streaming loader should be seamless.

maya: Exactly — WeightSource.Resolve will return either type: "safebox" or "file_shard". Loader chooses path. No change to public APIs.

anya: Security/compliance: private deployments need KMS/HSM integration. If safebox supports encryption-at-rest per-chunk, we need an encrypted-header marker and KMS key id. That will complicate range reads if we can't decrypt in-place.

simon: Decrypt-on-read is fine. For mmap candidates we can keep that path only for unencrypted safeboxes. Encrypted safeboxes must be read+decrypt into cache. We'll record flag in descriptor.

kevin: Also quotas: storing microbundles may raise cache pressure. We should expose per-safebox eviction hints in index (popularity_score estimate or hotness_hint) so optimizer can prefetch smartly.

maya: Good UX: extend existing warmup policies with a new hint: index.hint_priority (0..10) and per-chunk hotness. We can piggyback on the existing warmup coordinator.

josh: Anything on checksums/versioning? We must avoid silent mismatches.

maya: Header will include container_version (semver-ish), global checksum (SHA256), and per-chunk digest. Index has compatibility range. Loader must reject unknown container_version > supported version unless allow_unsafe flag is set.

anya: One more operation concern: pack creation speed. If we make packing expensive, pipeline will suffer for frequent model builds. We should provide fast pack mode (no compression, minimal rewrite) for CI artifacts and a slow pack mode (zstd+dedupe) for release bundles.

simon: We can reuse current model-bundle toolchain as a plugin to produce safebox. Default in CI: "fast". Release pipeline: "optimized".

kevin: Dev note: I'll add a fast-path reader in the runtime to read only the chunk index (first 64KB), then prefetch top-k big tensors via async IO. I have a prototype patching approach that avoids locking the global cache during warmup.

maya: Action items:
- kevin: push prototype reader + microbench into experiment branch by EOD Fri (1789003000 expected).
- simon: sketch WeightDescriptor additions and update WeightSource.Resolve contract (PR).
- anya: write brief doc on atomic swap lifecycle for safebox + shared cache.
- josh: add packing modes to model-bundle CLI and a minimal spec for microbundles.

anya: +1. Also add a short compatibility test that validates safebox -> fallback streaming on tiny host.

maya: Thanks team. If no objections I'll land a short RFC-note in the weights-loading RFC thread and we can sync next week. :thumbsup:

simon: SGTM :+1:

kevin: Will follow up with perf numbers and a small diag script to visualize chunk layout.

ci-bot: [ci] 1789002500 - safebox/prototype build passed unit tests

josh: If anyone wants to poke the prototype locally ping me for the build artifact.

maya: Closing loop here. We'll keep iteration lightweight and aim for backward-compatible rollout. Thanks. :coffee:
